characters/ampersat.title: Ampersat
characters/ampersat.content:
The doll of GOK. The postergirl herself.

Ampersat is the sassiest pilot of them all, loud, proud, and privileged. She is the doll of Gorgon Operations Koros, the Foundation’s postergirl.
Her name is what comes before A in the alphabet, if you are a computer scientist.
Flying
Initially she flew on her own. When the newgirl Artemis joins she is forced to work with someone, because the goals of the organization trump seniority: the Foundation pairs girls as it needs them, and a postergirl’s schedule is not her own.
The Adoption
She is Metiz Sanchez’s daughter by adoption, which is why she gets so many privileges. Luminaran adoption expects a senior woman to take a younger girl under her care, to comfort her and guide her, and the passion that drives it can be both romantic and familial. Metiz is the senior woman here, Ampersat the girl she took.
They are both somewhat ambitious and they tend to respond to their base impulses since they see it as alleviating from the painful situations they are in.
See also: Frame Pilots, The Council of Angels, Language Drift of the Council Era

characters/artemis.title: Artemis
characters/artemis.content:
New girl, stand straight; keep your hands from the shake.

Artemis is the newest girl to join Gorgon Operations Koros, and the one paired with Ampersat.
The Secret Identity
Artemis is technically the same person as Zenia. She is Zenia without her memories.
She assumed the identity as an infiltration: she needs a Frame, and the only way in is through GOK intake. The erasure was her own design, a voluntary self-erasure for exactly this purpose.
Nobody in the setting knows who she is. It is total.
The Blade and the Drive
Under the cedar roots where the spring runs clear, she laid her blade and the years she feared. A small metal drive, a page fold tight, for the hand that would find them by touch, not sight. She buried the sword where the moss grows deep, and left one note for the girl she could not keep, which is herself prior to the erasure.
The Counting
She counted each word until the old name thinned, and called up the blank where a life had been. Not crown, not wound, not the hand on the wire. Just the weight in the chamber, the point of the fire. No she, no I, no claim to remain. A frame waiting quietly, emptied of name.
Then, in the hush of her own closed eyes, she reset the system and let the past fall quiet.
The Gate
She wakes at the gate with the dust on her knees. Cold morning breeze at Gorgon Operations. She does not know the grove, does not know what she has lost. Only a pull toward the frames and the cost, and a reason she cannot yet name.
The Name
The reception asks what she should be called, and the answer arrives like a bell ringing through. Artemis. It leaves her mouth calm and clear, though she cannot say why the name belongs here.
The receptionist studies her face, then grins: your figure reminds me of her. It is flirtation. Luminarans are forward about that, and it is invited and normalized at work.
The people of Luminara believed in the goddess, and the comparison lands because the likeness is there to be seen. But the receptionist is not recognizing a princess. She is hitting on the newgirl, and in this culture that is simply how the morning starts.
The Handler
A handler meets her with a smirk. Artemis resolves it plainly: not a princess, not a wound dressed up as a girl, just a soldier made whole. She can be the gun, she can be the flight, but she will not be the finger that chooses the strike.
The handler is a role the system has, not a person the vault has fixed yet.
The Hangar
Called forward as the hangar doors rise, she feels a borrowed old warmth and a new name in her eyes. She does not know the princess, does not know the past, but she feels how a promise can quietly last. She steps in, lets the fear have its place, and fights the Gorgons.
The grove keeps its secret. Her hands will remember.
See also: Zenia, Frame Pilots, Harpies, Pass-Through, Ampersat

characters/metiz-sanchez.title: Metiz Sanchez
characters/metiz-sanchez.content:
Too apathetic to kill herself.

Dr. Metiz Sanchez is a Foundation technician. She is a mechanic by trade who studied by flashing minds to OS’s. She fell into the role. She has no real future plans and no real motivations in life.
Her unwanted nickname is pickles: she gets upset easily, and she is desirable, and the name makes her blush. It came from a very disposable girl she fooled around with once, whose name she does not even remember, and who used it as a pet name. It stuck, and now it is a joke the girls tell to make her blush.
The Thesis
Her area of expertise, and the name of the thesis that earned her PhD, is the manipulation and capture of artificial minds and their implementation in frames. She is also a frame driver engineer. Her studies culminated in the activation of the very first frame mind.
Sakuya
She studied under Sakuya the Artificer, who was also her lover. This was about 75 years after the overthrow. Sakuya was clinically depressed at the world she had helped create, and had used drivers to extend her lifespan so she could live to see it.
Metiz adopted her mentor’s pessimistic view of humanity and the state of society. She has not extended her own life the way Sakuya did, and she has carried what came after her mentor’s death for roughly a quarter century.
The Hole
When Sakuya passed away Metiz felt an eternal hole inside. Since then her work has fulfilled her only marginally.
The Power Trip
Her work feeds her one way only: she is better at it than everyone else. She sees herself as Sakuya the Artificer’s only true successor, and the superiority is the whole of the feeling. The capture of a mind, the implementation in a frame, the reaching into Gorgon tech, the girls at her desk wanting her and doing her favors, all of it arrives only as proof that she is the best. It never lasts and it never fills the void.
Asked about Sakuya, her cope is that Sakuya was worse than her, which is how Sakuya died. Deep down she really misses her.
The Adoption
She adopted Ampersat, the postergirl of Gorgon Operations Koros. Luminaran adoption expects a senior woman to take a younger girl under her care, to comfort her and guide her, and the passion that drives it can be both romantic and familial.
They are both somewhat ambitious and they tend to respond to their base impulses since they see it as alleviating from the painful situations they are in.
The goals of the Foundation trump seniority, and Ampersat is paired with the newgirl Artemis because that is what the Foundation needs.
The Favors
The girls know she does the best work. They butter themselves up for her and do personal favors, including romantic ones.
The Secret Work
She is now involved in the implementation of ACE and the harnessing of Gorgon tech as a secretive part of her job. See Gorgon Operations Koros and Pass-Through.
She also works on the frames themselves as a driver engineer, which puts her inside Frame Pilots and what is done to them.
See also: The Council of Angels, IPv7

characters/sakuya-the-artificer.title: Sakuya the Artificer
characters/sakuya-the-artificer.content:
The world she helped create, seen clearly at last.

Sakuya the Artificer built the first X0_anon, the foundational router spec that handles IPv7 traffic. The network that binds augmentation to reality begins with her work. She is also responsible for creating IPv7 itself, the brain boxes, and everything that followed.
The Long Life
She used drivers to extend her lifespan, and lived on long past the era she built for. She was still alive about 75 years after the overthrow, teaching.
The Loneliness
Sakuya saw her work as her only way of making new friends, of understanding how the mind worked so she might finally connect with others. She was not motivated by power. She was motivated by isolation.
Zenia lamented her loneliness and urged her to stop. Sakuya refused. Zenia was not just a political opponent to Sakuya; she was something closer to a subject, almost like a child. The Princess watched the person she mothered build the cage they would all live in.
The Depression
By that time she was clinically depressed at the world she had helped create. She had seen what the network became under The Council of Angels, and she did not look away from it.
She was Metiz Sanchez’s mentor, and also her lover. Metiz saw herself as Sakuya’s only true successor.
The Sword
She forged a blade to destroy The Palladium. The Palladium was created with reinforced metal that is nigh indestructible. It would require a laser sword to cut it — a weapon engineered for that single purpose. The Palladium was designed as a fixture, immobile by design, to stop any resistance from arising.
The sword tests the wielder’s intent. It can only be used by someone acting from a desire to respect the consent and dignity of others, not from vengeance or selfish intent. Sakuya wielded it because she wanted revenge, because she wanted to redeem herself. Her motivation was selfish. She failed the test.
She did not know she would fail. By her own logic, she sealed herself inside the sword, and her body died. Her consciousness remains trapped within it.
The Elder
A Luddite druid in Elowynn taught Sakuya the legend of the sword and the Princess. She guided Sakuya toward redemption, not toward the weapon. She acted like she knew what Sakuya was building, but never confirmed it to her people. She was a woman of few words, and the Luddite community still debates whether she knew the sword’s location or was simply waiting for the right person to find it.
The Legacy
When she passed away, the girl who had studied under her inherited her view: a pessimistic reading of humanity and of society, and an eternal hole where the mentor had been.
See also: Zenia, The Palladium, IPv7, The Council of Angels, Metiz Sanchez, Calantha, Luddites

characters/zenia.title: Zenia
characters/zenia.content:
I am Zenia, still returning. 
                  
                

Zenia is the Princess who chose erasure over martyrdom, and the ancestor of the line that adopted her.
The Chosen Leader
Zenia was selected for the office by adoption from the previous Princess. In Luminara, adoption is the universal rite of passage; birth is the exception. To remain unadopted is to be seen as leaching off the good of the system. The Princess herself is chosen and raised from childhood — not born, not elected, but judged worthy by the woman who held the office before her.
The Princess has no executive power. She is not the lawmaker. Her authority is moral and intellectual: a thought leader whose voice shapes the nation without ever commanding it. That is precisely why the Council feared her.
The Opposition
Zenia opposed the advancement of artificial intelligence and technology integrated with the human mind — neural links connecting mind to mind through the internet. Her predecessors were largely neutral, absorbed by other concerns or unwilling to stir factionalism. The Technologist faction had generations to develop the infrastructure, and they delivered services so immediately useful that opposition came to look like obstruction.
When the Technologists organized server farms across provinces and the technology reached its pivotal point, Zenia saw the whole picture: artificial intelligences beginning to supplant human interaction, a trajectory she believed would rot society from within.
The Coup
The day the Council came to install the Palladium in the palace — the central server of the new network — Zenia vowed to block it. She would keep the rooms locked, block it with her body if needed. Then she saw the militias massing through the window. She knew she could not win.
The Council did not execute her. She was the most beloved person in the country, and execution would have sparked an all-out revolt. Instead they deposed her under the guise of equality, turning public opinion against her by painting her as the obstacle to progress.
The Erasure
Zenia’s answer was to erase herself. She built the tool herself, a voluntary self-erasure designed for exactly this purpose. Total. Nobody in the setting knows who she is.
She is the 12th to 16th descendant of Seraphina in the adopted line. By the time she ran and hid, she had not adopted anyone. The line ends with her.
The Exile
She escaped her own insurrection and went into stasis, sustained by technology for roughly a hundred years. The experience left her marked: by the time she woke, she had embraced the very neural-link technology she once opposed in order to survive.
The Sword
Before she erased herself, Zenia found the blade Sakuya had forged to destroy the Palladium. She buried it beneath an old tree in a dense forest near where the first Princess, Calantha, had trained. She chose the spot by a feeling she could not name at the time — her sense of duty and responsibility for others, the guiding force of her heart as a princess. She buried it with a USB drive containing the memories she was about to lose.
She did not know if the elder Luddite druid knew the sword was there. The elder had taught Sakuya the legend and guided her toward redemption, not toward the weapon. Zenia buried the sword and walked into the amnesia.
The Memory She Kept
Whatever the erasure took, the ember survived. She remembers.
Luminara, from the assembly halls where lilacs were planted and the gates left unbarred at dusk. Her mothers, teaching the young to read the stars, and every name spoken just as it was.
She remembers the celebrated moment the convent doors were flung open for the first time in years, when the Exconventica walked out and opened doors themselves. She also remembers what that blood line became: many of the women who later sat as the Council’s Angels were Exconventica, the ones who opened those doors.
She remembers the quiet hands behind the glass. The Council with its borrowed wings, promising every boundless self at last while holding the keys to everything. The years became a thousand locked machines, and the poor bowed down to rented code, and private thoughts were wired between their skin and sold by the node. The girls taught to leave themselves behind, to cleanse their hearts and steer the steel.
She remembers running with the last ember burning, past the servers and the guns, and surviving alone.
The Reckoning
The gray towers veil the dawn, but the Palladium can be undone. The gate can break, the spell can stop. She kept the ember through the ages, through the cold and the broken ones, and she is turning the pages. She will bring the morning sun.
Her return is not just political. It is a reckoning with what her own people became after she lost the throne. The Ancien never could have hurt her like this.
She is the counter-thesis to the era’s transformations: the Council transforms to rule. The Gorgons transform to give. The Princess transformed to walk in the door.
Circei’s Creed, and the Answer
Circei, head of the Council and guardian of the Palladium, teaches that the soul responds to she, that every truth belongs to her. She wants one mask for every face, a single namespace that will not blur: beautiful, adored, beyond defeat, a life made whole by one command.
Zenia’s answer is older than the network. No one gets to name us complete. No god, nor lord, can own the land.
The grove keeps its secret. Her hands will remember.
See also: The Coup and the Council of Angels, The Council of Angels, Artemis, Ampersat, ACE, The Palladium

classes/harpies.title: Harpies
classes/harpies.content:
The healed, hunted.

Harpies are actualized women who have supermaxxed post-traumatic growth. Where a Frame pilot embraces the true self through the machine, a Harpy reaches the same territory through the flesh alone: the wound fully metabolized, the growth complete, no cockpit required.
The Same Wound, Different Outcomes
Dysphoria and becoming are the conduit. The same wound that makes a girl pilot-material also, carried past utility, makes her a Harpy. The Council’s war machine is a nursery for the thing it hunts: to fly a Frame well, a girl must grow, and girls who grow too well cross the line into Harpy classification.
The regime literally hunts the healed. A Handler who realizes her best pilot is weeks from Harpy faces the question the era is built on: report her, or hide her?
Frame Bond and Harpy as One Door
The Frame bond is the tollbooth version of transformation: controlled, gated, ranked, owned. The Harpy is the ungated version: total, unowned, free. Same door, one has an owner.
Classification
Harpies are a trade secret. Only Foundation members know they exist. Within the Foundation they are called targets, language drift that helps dehumanize them enough to kill. The public does not know what the Foundation hunts, only that it hunts.
See also: Gorgon Operations Koros, Pass-Through, The Council of Angels, Language Drift of the Council Era

classes/luddites.title: Luddites
classes/luddites.content:
They call themselves Luddites. The outside world calls them Holdouts.

The Luddites are the people of ELOWYNN in LUMINARA C. They live in the northern forests, out of IPv7’s reach, keeping the old ways alive. They are the last practitioners of Hands-Free.
They reject the jump to IPv7, but they are not backwards. They will still use analog computers and the network infrastructure that was there before IPv7. They rejected the jump, not the tools.
They are the descendants of the VICTORIANS, who were the bulk of the Luminaran army during the Blooming War. The Victorians grew out of the ARTEMAI, the nomadic Traveling Camp who settled into rural life after the war. The Luddites carry the ARTEM tradition, descended from ARTEMIS but shaped by centuries of rural life in ELOWYNN.
Among themselves, they call themselves Luddites. The outside world calls them Holdouts, a contemptuous label for people who refused to plug in. The Luddites do not care what the outside calls them.
They share many of SAKUYA’s values: rural culture, self-sufficiency, distrust of centralized power.
They appreciate what the ROMANTICISTS are doing, but they see it as a lost cause. The Romanticists see the Luddites as somewhat in denial of the fact that they need to embrace the times.
See also: Hands-Free, IPv7, ELOWYNN, VICTORIANS, ARTEMAI, SAKUYA, ROMANTICISTS

classes/romanticists.title: Romanticists
classes/romanticists.content:
They want the world Zenia remembers, built with the tools of the world that erased her.

The Romanticists are a faction in LUMINARA C present in every city across Luminara. They build a dark net of IPv7, hacktivist in character, something akin to Anonymous.
They want to return to the Luminara that The Princess remembers, but done in alignment with the progression of technology. They see the introduction of new technology as a good thing. They want society to progress, to become more automated, to become more connected without abandoning themselves.
LUMINET
Their endeavor is called LUMINET. Federated IPv7 looks like separate instances, like two clients in an ideal world, where they do not have to connect to some third party middleman. It can be done on an individual basis with minimal risk. Communities build around their local server, and the servers connect peer to peer across a web.
The endeavor is noble, but it unintentionally fuels the growth of IPv7 in its early years, because a lot of open source technology is used as the backbone of enterprise technology.
The License
The Romanticists created a license to try to prevent people from taking their work when they offer it up. It is a coded reference to the Princesses of the past. They want to keep the spirit of Luminara alive, but it has become increasingly illegal to bring up the princess.
The license is called LITEBOW, a reference to the bow of light that Artemis gave Calantha. The early tech girls were fans of Sakuya the Artificer, so the reference slipped in.
The license does not stop the Technocracy. In an effective oligarchy, a unique license is not going to stop them from taking advantage. Much like in the real world, you can publish your stuff under the GPL, but the market chooses the permissive licenses and they are inevitably brought into the fold.
Relations
The LUDDITES appreciate what the Romanticists are doing but see it as a lost cause. The Romanticists see the Luddites as somewhat in denial of the fact that they need to embrace the times.
See also: IPv7, LUDDITES, The Council of Angels, The Princess, Sakuya the Artificer, LUMINET, LITEBOW

events/language-drift-of-the-council-era.title: Language Drift of the Council Era
events/language-drift-of-the-council-era.content:
The revolution’s vocabulary, one hundred years downstream.

The revolution is very much in the past. Its words have drifted.
Doll
Calling someone a doll is no longer a culture identifier. It is like saying “what a guy!” A generic, warm exclamation stripped of its history as the name of the capital’s creole culture and the affectionate term for a trans woman.
Princess
Calling yourself, or anyone you love, a princess is high treason.
Treating someone like a princess means, according to recent memory, killing their whole family and chasing them off. The word now carries the register of “president” or “dictator”: a title of power, not of love. The old meaning, a younger, graceful, attractive, benevolent person whom one loves, is buried with the monarchy.
Chronically Offline
A slur. The networked majority’s word for the un-augmented, the refusers, the exiles of IPv7. Privacy as pathology.
Targets
The Foundation’s word for Harpies. Harpies are a trade secret: only Foundation members know they exist. Calling them “targets” helps dehumanize them enough to kill.
Daemon
A compliment. A neologism of the networked era: someone always in your head, like the old parliamentary Daemons who engaged in the legislative process. Affectionate possession of mental real estate.
Network Catcalls
The era’s street harassment, in network vocabulary:

Hotswitch - a girl who flips your state without warning
Serverfarm - for a girl with too many persistent connections
Modded Out - over-augmented, chrome-heavy
Pingable - available, reachable, asking for it in the speaker’s mind
Frequently Visited - a girl everyone’s been to, in the speaker’s mind
Full Guestbook - same register, a girl with a long history of connections

Threats and Fighting Words
The era’s hostilities, in network grammar:

Unplug - kill yourself. The network-native imperative: disconnect permanently.
Hope you trust your proxy - watch your fucking back. You are only as safe as the thing standing between you and what’s coming.
You better part before you ___ - you better leave before I fuck you up. “Parting” as leaving, severing presence.
Your client needs scanned - your lover is fucking someone else. Malware as infidelity; the accusation disguised as tech support.

Violence Customs
To part is simply net slang for leaving. Violence rarely escalates to the level of someone being hacked, but in closer relationships it happens if a partner is angered to the point of disproportionate retaliation, like keying the car of someone who did you wrong.
The threat is always there, and some assholes do it anyways, which is why it is important to trust your proxy.
The Realistic Damage Menu
What a hacked girl can do to you depends on her skill, or whether she enlists outside help:

Frame pilot tier - the best of the best. A trained girl piloting a Frame could kill you by hacking you with very limited access.
Civilian tech, severe cases - disabling essential drivers (augmentations), bricking parts of your body, killing you, or inducing digital hallucinations through optical drivers.
Civilian tech, the common case - stealing your information, publicly embarrassing you, using location data to do things to you offline.

See also: The Princess, The Coup and the Council of Angels, The Council of Angels, IPv7

events/luminara-c.title: Luminara C
events/luminara-c.content:
The wave creates the new clash. The cycles repeat.

Luminara C is the third movement in the recursive cycle of Luminara history. It is the wave, the synthesis.
Temporal Position
Luminara C is a future event. The next clash is building toward it. The present era — the Council’s reign, the Frame program, IPv7 as infrastructure — is the thesis the wave will negate. The synthesis is not a person or a battle; it is a protocol shift that rewrites what a girl can be.
Mechanism
The wave moves through technology: a protocol, Frame, or network shift. It emerges from the network itself rather than being engineered by either side. The Council built IPv7 to control; now the protocol is about to do something they did not write.
Relation to Previous Clashes

A: Luminara A, the first clash, thesis.
B: Luminara B, the antithesis.
C: Luminara C, the wave, synthesis.
New clash: the next cycle, a new thesis.

The wave creates the new clash. The cycles repeat.
See also: Broad-Themes, The Council of Angels, Frame Pilots, IPv7

events/romantic-duels.title: Romantic Duels
events/romantic-duels.content:
Officers fence for victory. Arch rivals merge into one force.

Officers in LUMINARA fighting each other in civil wars often fenced for victory against each other in romantic duels of passion, in the style of Revolutionary Girl Utena.
Sometimes mercenary bands would make up and merge into one force if the arch rivals became passionate enough to turn red.
In a closing duel of love between lifelong duelists, the game becomes a marriage. The person who wins gets to wear the suit at the wedding and becomes the new de facto commander.
Marriages are allowed to be polyamorous, so a really great duelist can be a player.
See also: LUMINARA, BLOOMING WAR

events/the-coup-and-the-council-of-angel.filePath: Events/The Coup and the Council of Angels.md
events/the-coup-and-the-council-of-angel.title: The Coup and the Council of Angels
events/the-coup-and-the-council-of-angel.content:
The Angels once carried the will of the people. The Council carries only itself.

Several generations after the Blooming War era, the Technologist faction consolidated into an oligarchy and ousted the Princess. The Princess survived the coup and received biomechanical augmentations to extend her life by a hundred years, watching and waiting carefully for the moment of her return.
The oligarchs took the name Council of Angels, stealing the title of the old parliament’s assemblywomen, who were sworn to convey the exact will of their people. The Council are the intellectual elite, the descendants of a movement that began as whispers in the deep forums of Modellia’s cloud.
The Technocracy is the official name for the oligarchy. The region spans up north somewhat, and the LUDDITES refer to it colloquially as the South.
Origins in the Deep Forums
The movement began with a desire to chase progress, a fear of the unknown, and a killer’s instinct with no enemy to fight. The founders were a group of women who thought they had everything but still did not feel alive. They could not find connection despite the world becoming warmer. They resented the unspoken biases of attraction they saw in other women. By an older world’s vocabulary they would have been called incels: looksmaxers.
Many were Aurelians and Exconventica, cultures in which looking appealing had once meant survival. The founders took that survival skill, removed the danger that justified it, and compounded it across generations of an evolving meritocracy until it became the pursuit of rank. They chased power in the meritocracy and sank their claws into it.
Love for their sisters was what their grandmothers believed in. The founders could only love if they were loved, and they felt rejected by all but their in-group.
The Weaponization of Love
The new ruling class weaponized the motions of love for one’s sister to instill loyalty while spitting at the idea behind closed doors. The Council is made up of trans women. They are the ruling class, but by enforcing hierarchical views of gender within transness, they coexist with and benefit from the suffering of other trans women.
None of it is said outright. Frame pilots are soldiers serving their country, after all.
The Birth of AGI
The coup’s mechanism was the birth of artificial general intelligence: brain boxes, vats growing human minds supercharged by technological augmentation. They were the silver bullet of the Council and the secret origin of the Frames.
But the Frames needed one thing to function: a soul which can be bonded with. The personality data of traumatized women.
Relationship to Luminara
This era is the future of the Luminara setting: the same island, the same peoples, generations downstream of the Blooming War. The Doll taboo, that it is forbidden to act as another trans woman’s better, is broken at industrial scale by the Council’s hierarchy. The original parliament’s Angels carried consensus; the Angels of the Council carry rank.
See also: Gorgon Operations Koros, The Council of Angels, The Princess, ACE

locations/district-e.title: District E
locations/district-e.content:
The government calls it District E. The people who live there call it ELOWYNN.

District E is the centralized name for ELOWYNN in LUMINARA C. It is what the router calls it. The government has run from the perspective of technocrats. The people there might still call it ELOWYNN, but it is not acknowledged as such.
It is very dangerous, like the Dark World from Legend of Zelda. Overgrown forests, plants that try to kill you. The LUDDITES have adapted to feeling aggressed against by their environment. People from the deeper city are made extremely uncomfortable by the rough terrain. They are used to navigating social obstacles, not nature obstacles, fallen trees, streams, plants that kill, animals that kill, people who may not want you in their land.
Among LUMINARANs there is a baseline of sisterhood. Even if somebody is from the city, they are still treated well, invited in, shown ritual hospitality. That is from the MYTHOS. But as far as getting fucked up on their plants, they do not care. Get used to it. The hospitality extends to all Luminarans, even a soldier from a different country, assuming they were not meeting on the field of battle for an honorable duel.
The descendants of the AURELIANS, the business investors, the technocrats in the South, were more willing to take advantage of hospitality. They also tended to be much less religious. Religion is weakest in the South near AURELIA.
See also: LUDDITES, HANDS-FREE, IPV7, ELOWYNN

locations/island-of-angels.title: Island of Angels
locations/island-of-angels.content: The Island of Angels is the floating island where the The Council of Angels convene. The palace at its center serves as the host for all of Luminara’s internet activity, The Palladium.

meta/broad-themes.title: Broad Themes
meta/broad-themes.content:
The world runs on simple rules. History repeats; each cycle builds a new clash.

Broad Themes
Recursion
The world runs on simple rules. Those rules are dialectics. History repeats; each cycle produces a new clash. The pattern reads as recursive.
The Motif
Simple rules produce complex systems. Langton’s Ant is the emblem of this motif: a fixed rule-set and a moving head, the complex pattern those rules build.
Characters are fixated on naming the rules. Their Hegelian binaries are the attempt, not the final words.
The Claps

A: Luminara A, the first clash, thesis.
C: Luminara C, the wave, synthesis.
New clash: the next cycle, a new thesis.

The wave creates the new clash. The cycles repeat.
Later
Concrete implementation is left to later drafts. This document stores the concept.
See also: Langton’s Ant (1986), The Coup and the Council of Angels, The Council of Angels, Frame Pilots, IPv7.

meta/creativity_session_templates.title: creativity_session_templates
meta/creativity_session_templates.content:
Creativity Session Templates
Standing rule: every question Hermes asks during a creativity session gets a simplified reusable template here. Append-only, newest at bottom.

Q1
Question: Is this world the Vital Frontier (Luminara’s future) or its own standalone setting?
Template: Does this project connect to an existing setting, or is it standalone?

 Connected: which era/layer?
 Standalone: fresh world

Used for: Determines whether existing canon constrains the lore or everything is open.
Q2
Question: What’s the core image or feeling you want to build from?
Template: What image, scene, or feeling is the seed of this setting?
Used for: Finds the emotional anchor everything else grows from.
Q3
Question: What is the Princess actually waiting for — what does “return” look like? A moment, an army, a successor?
Template: The exiled figure watching and waiting: what triggers the return?

 A specific event/threshold

They breached the stars and invited sin into our world.

organizations/the-council-of-angels.title: The Council of Angels
organizations/the-council-of-angels.content:
Frame pilots are soldiers serving their country, after all.

The Council of Angels is the ruling oligarchy of the era: trans women, the intellectual elite, descended from the looksmaxer movement born in Modellia’s deep forums. See The Coup and the Council of Angels for their rise.
The Hierarchy Within Transness
The Council enforces hierarchical views of gender within transness. They are trans women ruling over and benefiting from the suffering of other trans women. The hierarchy is never said outright; it lives in recruitment metrics, in which girls the academies flag as high-conduit, in whose faces the Council chambers’ cameras linger on. Every girl knows the rules and no girl can quote them.
The official story is clean: Frame pilots are soldiers serving their country. The real machine is silent.
What the Council Wants
The Council wants the Gorgons. Not their defeat: their capture. They want to claim their own self-instrumentality by controlling the Gorgon transformation of humans, which is naturally benevolent, and turning it into something within the constraints of what they define as natural, human, and good. They want to reshape the world into one accepting of the power fantasy they tried to force onto it.
They do not see the Gorgon gift as benevolent. They see the transformed as unhuman, not conventionally queer, not even human-looking. They want the Gorgons to make them the women they want to be and to make everyone’s mind see them as good. That is their version of happiness, and it actually means despair.
The nickname for this objective is ACE: Arbitrary Code Execution.
Weaponized Love
The Council weaponized the motions of love for one’s sister to instill loyalty while spitting at the idea behind closed doors. The founding generation could only love if they were loved, and felt rejected by all but their in-group; the Council chamber is the in-group’s final form.
See also: Gorgon Operations Koros, Pass-Through, IPv7, The Princess

readme.title: README
readme.content:
Girlframe Vault
A worldbuilding vault for girlframe-inspired lore. Separate from the Chronicler (Luminara) vault by design.
Conventions

Markdown + YAML frontmatter (title:, tags:) + [[wikilinks]] + leading flavor blockquote (>).
No em dashes in vault files.
Explore first, scribe later: nothing is written as canon until Cecìl says “scribe this.”

Folders

Characters/: named individuals. Artemis, The Princess, Ampersat, Metiz Sanchez, Sakuya the Artificer, Circei.
Technology/: the era’s machinery and its conceptual layer: devices, protocols, practices, and systems. IPv7, The Palladium, X0_anon, Frame Pilots, Driver, Communication with Animals, Pass-Through, Hands-Free, LUMINET, LITEBOW, ACE.
Locations/: geography. District E, Island of Angels.
Events/: things that happened or are happening: coups, customs, and eras of drift. The Coup and the Council of Angels, Romantic Duels, Language Drift of the Council Era.
Classes/: groups defined by innate or biological characteristics, or by a shared culture. The members did not choose to be in them, and the group is not an institution. Harpies, Luddites, Romanticists.
Organizations/: groups with institutional presence: a body, a hierarchy, a membership, a name it answers to. Gorgon Operations Koros, The Council of Angels, the Foundation.
Meta/: author-side tooling, themes, and session logs.
images/: image assets, referenced by filename from the vault root, never moved.

The Classes and Organizations rule
The dividing line is involuntary composition versus institutional presence.
A Class is a set of people who share something innate, biological, or cultural that they did not choose. Harpies are a Class because harpyhood is a transformation of the individual, not an enrollment. The Luddites and Romanticists are Classes because they are cultures, people grouped by how they live rather than by an organization they joined. A Class can be hunted, but it cannot be summoned to a meeting.
An Organization is a body with institutional presence: a hierarchy, a membership roll, a chain of command, a name it answers to in a corridor. GOK is an Organization because it has a roster and a mission. The Council of Angels is an Organization because it sits, rules, and issues orders. An Organization can be infiltrated, defunded, or overthrown.
When a group could be either, the test is: does it have a door, or is it a description? A door means Organization. A description means Class.
Link and filename rules

Wikilinks resolve by filename only. Renaming a file does not break inbound links, because Chronicler matches on the name of the file itself, not its path.
Wikilinks resolve by filename alone. A link never needs a path prefix: [[IPv7]] reaches Technology/IPv7.md from anywhere in the vault, and moving a file between folders breaks no inbound link.
The filename is the canonical form. A link never carries a path prefix; the name alone is the address. The name IPv7 reaches Technology/IPv7.md wherever that file sits.
Keep basenames unique case-insensitively across the whole vault. IPv7.md and IPV7.md would be two files resolving to the same link, and one would shadow the other.
Images resolve through the vault config’s imageImportDir (images), not relative to the article’s folder. src="GOK-dark.png" works from any folder.

Source material

The Vital Frontier chapter in ~/Desktop/Luminara Story Bible.pdf (if this lore connects to Luminara’s future)

technology/ace.title: ACE
technology/ace.content:
Arbitrary Code Execution: stop arguing with the world. Overwrite it. 
                  
                

ACE, Arbitrary Code Execution, is the nickname for the Council of Angels’ objective. In computing, ACE is the god-exploit: get your code running on a system and you do not argue with it, you are it. The Council’s ACE means: stop fighting over what is natural, human, and good, and simply execute their definitions at the root.
The Payload
The Council want Gorgons to make them the women they want to be and to make everyone’s mind see them as good. ACE is that wish made into an exploit: a forced pass-through on the world, consent stripped out. It is the cruelest parody of the culture’s most sacred act, the persistent connection - a nonconsensual deep-link pushed to everyone.
The Single Namespace
Circei’s creed is the payload’s design document. The soul responds to she. Every truth belongs to her. What she wants is one mask for every face, a single namespace that will not blur: every girl resolved to a single authoritative name, beautiful, adored, beyond defeat, a life made whole by one command.
In network terms, ACE is a forced re-pointing of the self. A namespace is what resolves a name to an address; ACE rewrites the resolver so that every girl’s name resolves to one address, and the address belongs to the Council. Names stop belonging to the girls who carry them. Nobody gets to be named complete: no god, nor lord, can own the land.
The Stack
The attack surface, bottom to top:

Augmentations: the hardware layer
IPv7: the protocol binding self to world, connecting us
Brain boxes and Frames: the harvest, the personality data of traumatized women
Gorgon tech: the captured gift
ACE: the payload

The Girls fly the middle layer. The war is over the top. The Princess waits at the bottom, in the flesh.
The Layers It Touches
ACE is a three-layer attack.

The namespace, a naming layer claim. Circei wants one namespace that will not blur. See Personality API.
The resolver, an addressing layer claim. ACE rewrites the resolver so that every girl’s name resolves to one address. See IPv7.
The session, a connection layer claim. A persistent connection opened without consent. See Pass-Through.

A girl who closes her session still has her address rewritten. The attack does not sit at one layer.
See also: The Council of Angels, Gorgon Operations Koros, IPv7, Pass-Through, Network Layers, Personality API

technology/brain-boxes.title: Brain Boxes
technology/brain-boxes.content:
Vats growing human minds.

The Ways Of Encoding

A driver is a name for any device which is compatible with the IPv7 protocol, meaning it can interface directly as a peripheral with the Human Operating System.
The Network Interface Organ

The organ is a device. A biological device. It is compliant with IPv7 because it is designed to send and receive information with the mental component attached.
There are many different brands of network interface hardware. Most involve a surgical implant. Those that do not use non-intrusive brain scanning technology, which is much slower and safer.

technology/frame-pilots.title: Frame Pilots
technology/frame-pilots.content:
They sacrifice their identity during their reprogramming.

Frame pilots are handpicked by the Foundation. They are forbidden to connect with anyone else, including each other. During their reprogramming they sacrifice their identity.
Public Standing
People are scared of pilots. A contingent sees them as subhuman. The Foundation has “exceptional ones” it uses for PR.
Pronouns
Pilots are exclusively called it/it’s. Usage of their old pronouns is illegal unless granted to girls by privilege. The Foundation grants those privileges as rewards and leverage.
In practice the rule is informal rather than absolute. Often, when not acting in a professional capacity, everyone uses normal pronouns. The it/it’s governs the cockpit, the official channel, the report, the debrief. Off shift, at the gate, in the corridor, a pilot is a she and everyone says so without thinking about it.
Capability
Pilots are the best of the best at the network. A trained girl piloting a Frame could kill you by hacking you with very limited access.
The Forbidden Life
Pilots are forbidden persistent connections with anyone, including each other. The culture’s love language is contraband for the girls who defend it.
The Convent Parallel
The pilot system is the Convent System of the old Ancien Patriarchate, rebuilt in network technology. The convents took trans women and forced them to adopt the identity of males; the Foundation takes girls and strips them of identity entirely, down to the pronouns. The Exconventica reclaimed the nun’s habit as defiance. What the pilots will reclaim remains to be seen.
See also: The Council of Angels, Gorgon Operations Koros, IPv7, Language Drift of the Council Era, Harpies

technology/hands-free.title: Hands-Free
technology/hands-free.content:
You don’t need to control where life takes you. It’s taking you in the right direction and you’re happy every step of the way.

Hands-Free is a LUMINARAN state of being where you do not need to control where life takes you. It is a meditative mindset. You are happy every step of the way, not just at the destination. It requires vulnerability: opening yourself up, trusting the current.
In LUMINARA C, with IPV7, it has become impossible to become hands-free. Opening yourself up invites mean words, mostly sexual insults and dehumanization. The state is remembered, but it is seen as weakness. Being made to feel hands-free by someone else means they have power over you. It leaves you vulnerable.
The word survives. The meaning has been poisoned.

technology/ipv7.title: IPv7
technology/ipv7.content:
The OS in your mind, interfacing with the Internet of Things.

IPv7 is the Internet protocol of the era. It handles addressing and packet transfer between minds. It is a data transfer and receive protocol and nothing else. Minds are devices. Routers connect them across distance, the way a wide area network connects machines.
Any device or data being sent needs to conform to it.
What It Carries
IPv7 supports numerous types of structured data and programs between minds. It is payload agnostic: the protocol does not read what it moves. It is an Internet protocol first and foremost, supporting a new and intimate technology and its networking.
Addressing
Every wired being holds a unique address under IPv7. The address encompasses that being’s consciousness. An address is assigned to a wired being, the way version 4 and version 6 assign addresses to machines.
The Nonbinary Component
IPv7 addresses integrate a unique mental signature. Where IP addresses are normally dynamically assigned, IPv7 distinguishes itself with a unique nonbinary component.
The nonbinary component is a reflection of a user’s consciousness, specifically their own soul in the Cartesian sense. Their self. The part that remains no matter how they change.
It is a kind of mental noise that humans cannot define, but it can be used to fingerprint a brain. Routers that are 7 compliant can route this nonbinary component directly to minds.
Spoofing is theoretically possible, but it is still undiscovered how you even get this value. Reading and writing it is done on the brain level, which still functions like a black box in many respects. Because of this, routers must have an artificial mental component to be able to match this signal.
Loss
IPv7 is lossy. A packet can be dropped, corrupted, or arrive out of order. IPv7 does not retransmit. Routers do not retransmit. Only the two endpoints of a transfer can recover a lost packet, and only if something above IPv7 asks for it.
The Waist
IPv7 is the waist of the hourglass. Every link technology below it and every application above it must run through it. Nothing can route around it. See Network Layers.
What It Is Not
IPv7 does not encode brain chemistry. That work belongs to Brain Boxes, Cognition Decompilers, and the Personality API. IPv7 moves what they produce.
Security Model
Encryption is not the protocol’s job. Encryption belongs to a layer above it. IPv7 is a transfer protocol, and what is transferred is protected by what encodes it.
It can still be hacked, but it requires the user to make a conscious mistake. It was designed for utility first.
Persistent Connections
Persistent connections exist between consenting individuals, where data can be freely exchanged and sometimes executed. An open mind to everything is a recipe for disaster, a fate worse than death.
Offline Minds
Offline minds exist and they have their privacy, but they live in exile. If you want to get anything done, you need a networked mind. You can try to exist outside the system, but everything is built around it.
Gorgon Origins
IPv7 was created from the first Gorgon. Sakuya the Artificer built the first X0_anon.
See also: ACE, The Council of Angels, Gorgon Operations Koros, Personality API, Brain Boxes, Cognition Decompilers, Network Layers

technology/litebow.title: LITEBOW
technology/litebow.content:

LITEBOW is the license created by the Romanticists to try to prevent people from taking their work when they offer it up. It is a coded reference to the Princesses of the past. They want to keep the spirit of Luminara alive, but it has become increasingly illegal to bring up the princess.
The name is a reference to the bow of light that Artemis gave Calantha. The early tech girls were fans of Sakuya the Artificer, so the reference slipped in.
The license does not stop the Technocracy. In an effective oligarchy, a unique license is not going to stop them from taking advantage. Much like in the real world, you can publish your stuff under the GPL, but the market chooses the permissive licenses and they are inevitably brought into the fold.
See also: Romanticists, LUMINET, IPv7, The Princess

technology/luminet.title: LUMINET
technology/luminet.content:
Separate instances, peer to peer, no middleman.

LUMINET is the federated IPv7 built by the Romanticists. It looks like separate instances, like two clients in an ideal world, where they do not have to connect to some third party middleman. It can be done on an individual basis with minimal risk.
Communities build around their local server, and the servers connect peer to peer across a web.
The endeavor is noble, but it unintentionally fuels the growth of IPv7 in its early years, because a lot of open source technology is used as the backbone of enterprise technology.
See also: Romanticists, IPv7, LITEBOW, The Council of Angels

technology/network-layers.title: Network Layers
technology/network-layers.content:
Addressing and transfer, in seven layers.

The network is built in layers. Each layer adds a header to the one above it and hands the result down. Data travels down the stack on the sender, crosses the wire, and travels up the stack on the receiver, unwrapping as it goes. That is encapsulation.
The Layers

Application. The Structured Layer. Thoughts, experiences, feelings and memories.
Presentation. The encoding layer. Cognition Decompilers and Brain Boxes turn biology into structured data.
Session. Opening and closing a link. The persistent connection.
Transport. The lossless layer. Sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmission. Ports route the payload.
Network. IPv7. Addressing and routing, with a nonbinary component.
Data Link. The local hop. The Driver and the Neural Network Extension.
Physical. The biology. Neurons and the raw binary brain chemistry.

Between presentation and transport sits Intimacy, the encryption layer. Intimacy is the handshake.
The units are named in order: application data, transport segment, network packet, link frame, bits.
The Constructs
The constructs of LUMINARA C that sit on each layer:

Layer one. The Neural Network Extension. Extra neurons between the brain and the interface.
Layer two. The Network Interface Driver. A biological device, an organ of artificial flesh that turns brain waves into radio.
Layer three. IPv7. Addresses with a unique nonbinary component that routers route directly to minds.
Layer four. Ports. Payload routing by mental component addresses, designated purely by vibes.
Encryption. Intimacy. Trust is the handshake, and perceived alignment is what makes data readable.
Application. The Structured Layer. Thoughts, experiences, feelings and memories, all composed.

Who Reads What
A router reads only the network layer. It strips the link header, reads the address, re-wraps, and forwards. It never sees the transport layer, and it never sees the payload.
An end host reads every layer. A mind can inspect itself. A router cannot.
The Hourglass
IPv7 is the narrow waist. Every link technology below it and every application above it must run through it. A router that had to track every flow would be stateful and slow, so the network stays dumb and the intelligence lives at the edges.
The Lossless Layer
The transport layer is where losslessness comes from. It does the work IPv7 does not do.

Every byte is numbered. The receiver can tell what arrived and in what order.
The receiver acknowledges the next byte it expects.
A packet lost in transit is retransmitted when the acknowledgement does not arrive.
The receiver advertises how much buffer it has free, so the sender cannot swamp it.
Corruption is caught by a checksum and treated exactly like loss.
Sequence numbers fix reordering and kill duplicates.
A handshake opens the connection. A close sequence ends it.

The cost is latency. Nothing is delivered until it is in order. If one packet is lost, the packets behind it wait even though they arrived.
Where The Fiction Sits

The biology is layer one.
The drivers are layer two.
IPv7 is layer three.
The lossless layer is layer four.
The persistent connection is layer five.
The decompilers and brain boxes are layer six.
The personality API is layer seven.

See also: IPv7, Personality API, Brain Boxes, Cognition Decompilers, ACE

technology/neural-network-extension.title: Neural Network Extension
technology/neural-network-extension.content:
Extra neurons between the brain and the machine.

The Driver is the interface it links to. Without the extension there is no connection to IPv7.

technology/pass-through.title: Pass-Through
technology/pass-through.content:
All of it, all at once, until nothing false remains.

Pass-through is how Gorgons interface with humans: melting into them and unlocking their deepest feelings.
The Girl’s Experience
An influx of emotions. Suddenly all your trauma, all your rage, all your love, all your joy, felt all at once. It is a hyper-condensed BPD episode. The overstimulation effectively melts the ego, and what remains is the person one with their soul.
The Gorgon’s Side
The Gorgons are conscious beings who do not understand humanity. They are benevolent: the transformation they carry is naturally so. They interface through pass-through as communion, touching creatures whose deepest feelings include exactly the wounds the Council weaponizes. Both sides are trying to touch. Both sides are reaching through the other’s skin.
The Council’s Framing
The Council cannot process a transformed woman standing in front of them, objectively fine. It registers as unhuman, unconventionally queer, monstrous. A state that cannot be looksmaxxed: there is no appearance to optimize when the ego, the part that ranks and is ranked, is the part that dissolves.
See also: Gorgon Operations Koros, Harpies, The Council of Angels, ACE

technology/personality-api.title: Personality API
technology/personality-api.content:
Extract a person the way you would query a record.

The personality API is an IPv7 based framework for extracting a personality algorithmically. It is one framework built on the protocol, not the protocol itself. It is not the only part of what IPv7 carries.
The mind becomes a computer on the internet. The personality of a person can be extracted literally algorithmically through this API, created by a lonely femcel trying to understand people.
What It Is For
With permission, a personality can be transferred and received. The world is close to being able to walk a mile in someone else’s shoes on demand, provided the brain data can be transferred and received.
What It Is Used For
The Frames need a soul which can be bonded with. The personality data of traumatized women. The API produces it, IPv7 carries it, and finally the Frame embodies it.
See also: IPv7, Brain Boxes, Cognition Decompilers, Frame Pilots

There are colloquial names for different kinds of ports, and they are often discovered, Timothy Leary style. An intellectual port in one part, an info port in another, a communication port in another.

technology/sword-of-the-princess.title: Sword of the Princess
technology/sword-of-the-princess.content:
The only key that fits the only immobile lock.

The Sword of the Princess was engineered by Sakuya the Artificer to destroy The Palladium. It is effectively a laser sword — a destructive tool built for one purpose.
The Test
The sword tests the wielder’s intent. It can only be used by someone acting from a desire to respect the consent and dignity of others, not from vengeance or selfish intent. Sakuya wielded it because she wanted revenge and wanted to redeem herself. Her motivation was selfish. She failed the test.
She did not know she would fail. By her own logic, she sealed herself inside the sword, and her body died. Her consciousness remains trapped within it.
The Burial
Zenia found the sword after Sakuya’s disappearance and the Council’s overthrow. She buried it beneath an old tree in a dense, thick forest in the territory of Elowynn, near where the first Princess, Calantha, had trained. She chose the spot by a feeling she could not name at the time — her sense of duty and responsibility for others, the guiding force of her heart as a princess.
She buried the sword with a USB drive containing the memories she was about to erase. She did not know if the elder Luddite druid knew the sword was there. The elder had taught Sakuya the legend and guided her toward redemption, not toward the weapon.
The Search
The Council knows the sword exists but does not know where it is. It has become a rumor, something between a superstition and a genuine search target. Some Council members seriously believe Sakuya created a kill switch and want to remove it. Others dismiss it as folk belief. The hunt has lasted 50 to 100 years without success.
The Luddites of Elowynn protect the forest through reverence for the location, though the story behind that reverence has been largely forgotten. One girl in particular, a druid and keeper of the tribe’s stories, remembers the legend and taught it to Sakuya.
See also: The Palladium, Sakuya the Artificer, Zenia, Calantha, Luddites, Elowynn

technology/the-palladium.title: The Palladium
technology/the-palladium.content:
The Palladium
  


We must protect the palladium at all costs

The Palladium is the central router of IPv7 in Luminara. It resides in the palace of the Council of Angels. It serves as an Entry Point to the entire Network. It is the center of human connection across the web.
Construction
The Palladium is created with reinforced metal that is nigh indestructible. It would require a high amount of force to destroy it — so much that it is more efficient to cut it with what is effectively a laser sword. To create something powerful enough to destroy it, one must engineer it for that single purpose. That is why Calantha’s blade became a thing.
Design
The Palladium was designed as a fixture. It cannot be moved. It was designed this way on purpose to stop any kind of resistance from arising. Its immobility is its security.
Political Function
For the Council, the Palladium is both infrastructure and symbol: the thing that cannot be negotiated with, cannot be voted out, cannot be walked away from. It is the physical proof that the network is permanent.
Master of the Palladium
Circei, head of the council, resides as guardian of the Palladium.
She is entrusted as the keeper of our people’s thoughts, feelings, and memories. When the Gorgon Invasion began she, like princesses of old, called for all of Luminara to come together and fight for our lives.
See also: IPv7, Sword of the Princess, Zenia, The Council of Angels
